1.e4 d5 2.f4 dxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Qe2.strategy: Piles a second attacker on e4 against its single defender and eyes b5, where a check would also hit b7. Black has to add a defender or give the pawn back. The queen is exposed on e2, though: a bishop arriving on g4 hits it with tempo.
1.e4 d5 2.f4 dxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Qe2.name: Bird's Opening: Williams Gambit
1.e4 d5 2.f4 dxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Qe2.background: The Williams of the name is uncertain: the second edition of The Oxford Companion to Chess credits the nineteenth-century player Elijah Williams, but no game of his in this line is cited. William L. Williams, who wrote a 1997 monograph on the gambit, claimed to have originated it in 1975.

1.e4 d5 2.f4 dxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nge2.strategy: Develops the knight with Ng3 in mind, to attack e4 a second time while the queen stays at home. The price is a blocked king's bishop and clumsy coordination, and White is still a pawn down, so Black can develop calmly.
1.e4 d5 2.f4 dxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nge2.name: Bird's Opening: Williams-Zilbermints Gambit
